Thanks for the captures — I've triaged the PCAP and logs. Short summary of findings so far:

1) Path / peering behavior: the flows from Sorrento's edge intermittently traverse a peering path that transits a third-party inspection appliance operated by their cloud partner (seen as TTL hops and AS path). That appliance injects a transparent proxy (SNI-inspecting TLS proxy) for some flows which is causing additional handshake RTTs and occasional mid-handshake RSTs.

2) MTU/fragmentation: we see occasional PMTU blackhole behavior when packets leave the inspection appliance; some large SYN/ClientHello packets trigger fragmentation and then drop, causing retries and timeouts.

3) Our service logs show elevated 502/503 responses correlated with the handshake failures and upstream resets. No model runtime errors on our side.

Immediate mitigations I'd recommend:
- Ask Sorrento NOC to route traffic to our fallback peering (redwood-us-west-2) while we validate the appliance behavior.
- If possible, have their cloud partner configure a bypass for direct egress to our VIPs (bypass SNI inspection for our FQDNs).
- Lower MTU on Sorrento's edge to avoid fragmentation around the inspection appliance until the root cause is fixed.

Action items: Dev will pull netflow and infra-level BGP/peering events; I'll coordinate with Marissa for customer comms.

Vivek
Director, Infrastructure & SRE
Redwood Inference

I pulled the BGP and peering telemetry for the window Lydia reported. Findings:
- We observed a short-lived AS path change at 18:04 PDT that rerouted some traffic via the partner inspection appliance (AS64512) for ~23 minutes. Nothing on our fabric changed.
- The partner's proxy is terminating TLS for inspection and re-originating connections — their logs show a spike in SYN retransmits and 'fragmented packet dropped' events.

I've attached the raw proxy logs they provided (sorrento-proxy-logs-20270617.log). I've also raised INF-4921 to track follow-up with the partner and Sorrento.

Proposed immediate steps we can take (short window):
1) Enable automatic region fallback for Sorrento to route primary traffic to us-west-2 for 1 hour (we can flip via runtime config).
2) Offer a temporary credit for impacted requests for good will (Marissa to scope amount).
3) Coordinate with Eric (cc'd) from the cloud partner to disable SNI inspection for redwood.ai FQDNs while they fix MTU behavior.

I'll stand by for the runtime toggle if Marissa / Sofia approve.

Lydia — thanks for the captures and patience. Executive summary for your CISO and internal comms below, plus what we did to contain the impact.

Executive summary (for CISO):
- Incident: Between 18:04–18:27 PDT on 2027-06-17, Sorrento traffic to Redwood experienced intermittent TLS handshake failures and an elevated 5xx rate causing ~20 minutes of elevated latency and reduced throughput.
- Root cause (preliminary): Traffic from Sorrento transited a third-party inspection appliance in their cloud egress path which performs SNI-based TLS interception. The appliance had PMTU/fragmentation handling issues that caused handshake retries and connection resets for larger ClientHello frames, producing downstream 502/503s. No model or runtime issues were observed on Redwood's side.
- Containment executed: With Sorrento NOC we briefly redirected production traffic to a fallback peering (us-west-2) and coordinated with the cloud partner to suspend SNI inspection for redwood.ai domains. We also suggested a temporary MTU decrease on Sorrento's edge. These steps restored normal service within ~12 minutes of activation.
- Next steps:
  1) Sorrento / cloud partner to remediate inspection appliance MTU behavior and confirm no further AS path flaps (owner: Sorrento NOC / cloud partner).
  2) Redwood to keep INF-4921 open and run a 72-hour synthetic test from Sorrento endpoints to confirm stability (owner: Infrastructure).
  3) Redwood will issue a goodwill credit for impacted token usage while we complete root cause verification (owner: Sales Ops / Marissa).

Please let us know if you need a short formal RCA and timeline. We will stay on the ticket and update you as we confirm partner remediation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
